source: User-supplied ONiO characterization in the project conversation, 2026-10-05–2026-10-06; not independently verified against a revision-specific datasheet.
limitations: User-provided baseline, not manufacturer-verified electrical data. Silicon revision, package, measurement rail and temperature are unspecified.
The model has a logical harvesting input and a user-named VMAIN bidirectional storage port; physical package pins are unknown.
Whole-device radio states include a sleeping CPU. Do not add CPU or sleep baseline power to them.
CPU run powers use 22 µW/MHz with no added fixed baseline; this remains a model assumption.
Power is held constant within the stated range; voltage-dependent curves and the 3 V upper limit are not enforced by the current engine.
Transition durations require explicit timeline events; they are not automatically inserted by the engine.
BLE 2M/coded operation and TX powers other than 0 dBm remain uncharacterized.
Storage is an energy-balance approximation with constant harvesting efficiency. Cold-start dynamics, external output rails and battery-chemistry control remain uncharacterized.

vmain_storage.source: User statements in the project conversation, 2026-10-06: ONiO.zero supports energy storage attached at VMAIN, using a capacitor, supercapacitor or battery. The user separately confirmed a VMAIN minimum operating voltage of 250 mV and a maximum operating voltage of 3.3 V. The user confirmed that charging stops at 2.7 V. The user corrected the restart voltage to 2.2 V; the minimum operating voltage remains 250 mV. The user confirmed 85% harvesting input-to-VMAIN efficiency.
vmain_storage.note: Harvesting input power is determined by the source profile and converted at 85%; no fixed VMAIN charging power is invented. Charging stops at 2.7 V and device restarts at 2.2 V. The minimum operating voltage 0.25 V is used as a modeled cutoff, not an independently characterized shutdown threshold. Waiting power defaults to an uncharacterized zero estimate. Capacitor/supercapacitor energy is 0.5CV²; batteries use a user-configured linear voltage versus charge approximation. Package mapping, voltage-dependent losses, current transients, charging chemistry and output rails remain uncharacterized.
